'''Wendell Horace Moore Jr.''' ({{IPAc-en|w|ɛ|n|ˈ|d|ɛ|l}} {{respell|wen|DEL}};{{cite press release|title=2023-24 start of season NBA pronunciation guide|url=https://www.nba.com/news/2023-24-start-of-season-nba-pronunciation-guide|website=NBA.com|date=October 24, 2023|access-date=May 18, 2024}} born September 18, 2001) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for [[Virtus Bologna]] of the Italian [[Lega Basket Serie A]] (LBA) and the [[EuroLeague]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke Blue Devils]]. ==High school career== Moore attended [[Cox Mill High School]] in [[Concord, North Carolina]]. As a freshman in 2015–16, he started in all 29 games played and averaged 17.9 points, 8.6 rebounds, 3.3 assists and 1.8 steals to help his team to a 22–8 record and a sectional championship. As a sophomore in 2016–17, he started in all 33 games and averaged 25.0 points, 9.2 rebounds, 3.9 assists and 2.3 steals to help his team to a 27–6 record and a 3A state title. As a junior in 2017–18, he became the fastest player to score 1,000 career points in Cabarrus County public school history; averaged 25.4 points, 7.3 rebounds, 2.9 assists and 2.3 steals to help his team to a 29–3 record and a second straight 3A state title. ===Recruiting=== On October 8, 2018, Moore announced that he would attend [[Duke University]] and play for the [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Blue Devils]] during the 2019–20 season. Moore picked the Blue Devils over [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina]], [[North Carolina State Wolfpack men's basketball|NC State]], [[South Carolina Gamecocks men's basketball|South Carolina]] and [[Wake Forest Demon Deacons men's basketball|Wake Forest]].{{cite [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina]]. He hit a putback shot after a [[Tre Jones]] miss to give the Blue Devils a 98–96 win.{{cite news |last=Cobb |first=David |title=Duke vs. North Carolina score, takeaways: Blue Devils stun Tar Heels on Wendell Moore's buzzer-beater in OT |url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/duke-vs-north-carolina-score-takeaways-blue-devils-stun-tar-heels-on-wendell-moores-buzzer-beater-in-ot/live/ |access-date=February 9, 2020 |work=[[CBS Sports]] |date=February 8, 2020}} Moore scored a career-high 25 points on February 25, in a 113–101 loss to [[Wake Forest Demon Deacons men's basketball|Wake basketball: Wendell Moore and Joey Baker preview 2021-22 season |url=https://247sports.com/Article/Duke-basketball-Wendell-Moore-and-Joey-Baker-preview-2021-22-season-174057589/ |access-date=November Team.{{cite press release|url=https://theacc.com/news/2022/3/6/athlete-awards-acc-unveils-2021-22-mens-basketball-awards.aspx|title=ACC Unveils 2021-22 Men's Basketball Awards |publisher=[[Atlantic Coast Conference]] |date=March 7, 2022 |access-date=March 7, 2022}} On November 12, 2021, Moore recorded 19 points, 10 rebounds and 10 assists, making him the fifth player in Blue Devils history with a triple-double.{{Cite web |last=Murata |first=Michael |date=November 14, 2021 |title=And one: Wendell Moore Jr.'s triple-double headlines Duke's balanced performance against Army |url=https://www.dukechronicle.com/article/2021/11/duke-mens-basketball-army-veterans-day-weekend-showcase-player-of-the-game-wendell-moore |access-date=2022-04-24 |website=The Chronicle}} On April 2, 2022, Moore was named the winner of the [[Julius Erving Award]].{{Cite web |last=Hurewitz |first=Micah |date=April 3, 2022 |title=Wendell Moore Jr. named Julius Erving Award winner |url=https://www.dukechronicle.com/article/2022/04/duke-mens-basketball-wendell-moore-julius-erving-award |access-date=April 3, 2022 |website=[[Duke Chronicle|The Chronicle]]}} He declared for the [[2022 NBA draft]] and forgoed his college eligibility on April 21.{{Cite web |date=2022-04-22 |others=Contributed by The Associated Press |title=Duke Blue Devils captain Wendell Moore Jr. latest to declare for 2022 NBA draft |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/33781611 |access-date=2022-04-24 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}} ==Professional career== ===Minnesota Timberwolves (2022–2024) === Moore was selected by the [[Dallas Mavericks]] with the 26th overall pick in the [[2022 NBA draft]], and then traded to the [[Houston Rockets]] as part of a trade involving [[Christian Wood]], and then again to the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] in exchange for the 29th overall pick [[TyTy Washington Jr.]] and two future second-round picks.{{Cite web |date=June 24, 2022|title=Timberwolves Acquire Draft Rights to Forward Wendell Moore Jr. from the Houston Rockets |url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/timberwolves-acquire-draft-rights-to-forward-wendell-moore-jr-from-the-houston-rockets |access-date=June 28, 2022 |website=NBA}} ===Detroit Pistons (2024–2025)=== On July 6, 2024, Moore was traded to the [[Detroit Pistons]] alongside the 37th overall pick in the [[2024 NBA draft]] in exchange for the 53rd pick in the draft and some cleared salary.{{cite web|title=Timberwolves Acquire a Future Draft Pick and Cash Considerations|url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/timberwolves-acquire-a-future-draft-pick-and-cash-considerations|website=NBA.com|date=July 6, 2024|access-date=July 6, 2024}} He made 20 appearances (one start) for Detroit during the [[2024–25 NBA season]], averaging 3.2 points, 2.2 rebounds, and 1.2 assists. On February 6, 2025, Moore was waived.{{Cite web|title=Pistons waive former first-round pick|url=https://www.yardbarker.com/nba/articles/pistons_waive_former_first_round_pick/s1_14822_41711635|date=February 6, 2025|website=yardbarker.com}} ===Charlotte Hornets (2025)=== On February 15, 2025, Moore signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Charlotte Hornets]].{{cite web|title=Charlotte Hornets Sign Wendell Moore Jr. To Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/news/charlotte-hornets-sign-wendell-moore-jr-to-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=February 15, 2025|access-date=February 15, 2025}} He made 16 appearances for the Hornets, averaging 5.4 points, 3.2 rebounds, and 1.2 assists. ===Maine Celtics (2025)=== Moore was a training camp participant for the [[Boston Celtics]] ahead of the [[2025-26 NBA season|2025–26 NBA season]], but was waived as part of final roster cuts on October 16, 2025.{{Cite web |title=Report: Boston Celtics cut Jalen Bridges, Kendall Brown, and Wendell Moore |url=https://celticswire.usatoday.com/story/sports/nba/celtics/2025/10/17/report-celtics-cut-jalen-bridges-kendall-brown-and-wendell-moore/86747646007/ |access-date=October 23, 2025 |website=celticswire.usatoday.com |language=en}} He signed with the Celtics' [[NBA G League]] affiliates, the [[Maine Celtics]], for the 2025–26 season.{{Cite web |title=Maine Celtics Announce Opening Night Roster |url=https://maine.gleague.nba.com/news/roster-announced-110625 |access-date=2025-11-06 |website=Maine Celtics |language=en}} ===Second stint with Pistons (2025–2026)=== On November 10, 2025, Moore signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Detroit Pistons]].{{cite web | title=Wendell Moore Jr. signs Two-Way Contract with Detroit Pistons | website=The NBA G League | date=2025-11-11 | url=https://gleague.nba.com/news/wendell-moore-jr-signs-two-way-contract-with-detroit-pistons | access-date=2025-12-07}} ===Virtus Bologna (2026–present)=== On July 28, 2026, Moore signed with [[Virtus Bologna]] of the [[Lega Basket Serie A]] (LBA) and the [[EuroLeague]].{{Cite web|title=Virtus reinforces perimeter with Wendell Moore|url=https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/en/euroleague/news/virtus-reinforces-perimeter-with-wendell-moore/|date=July 28, 2026|website=euroleaguebasketball.net|access-date=July 29, 2026}}
